subject: gr-qc
title_original: QCD axion from broken scale symmetry
abstract: A consistent non-compact axion cosmology requires a non-periodic field, an effective field theory valid sufficiently above the inflationary scale, and a small non-QCD contribution to the potential that tilts the axionic vacuum landscape in order to trigger a timely domain-wall collapse. All conditions can be met by the dilaton -- the pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone boson of spontaneously broken approximate scale invariance.
title_relatable: The dilaton solves three stubborn problems with axion cosmology at once
hook: A single field — the dilaton from broken scale symmetry — simultaneously fixes the non-periodicity, UV validity, and domain-wall collapse problems that plague standard axion dark matter models.
summary: Standard QCD axion cosmology runs into three distinct technical obstacles: the axion field must be non-periodic, the effective theory must hold well above the inflationary scale, and a small explicit symmetry-breaking term is needed to collapse dangerous domain walls before they dominate the universe. Karananas and Shaposhnikov show that the dilaton — the pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone boson of spontaneously broken approximate scale invariance — satisfies all three requirements within a single coherent framework. The result reframes the dilaton not merely as a gravitational curiosity but as a natural host for axion physics, potentially connecting dark matter to the origin of mass scales in nature.
